source_text: Τῶν δ᾿ ἐν Ἰουδαίοις προφητῶν οἱ μὲν πρὸ τῆς προφητείας καὶ τῆς θείας κατακωχῆς ἦσαν σοφοὶ, οἱ δ᾿ ἀπ᾿ αὐτῆς τῆς προφητείας φωτισθέντες τὸν νοῦν τοιοῦτοι γεγόνασιν, αἱρεθέντες ὑπὸ τῆς προνοίας εἰς τὸ πιστευθῆναι τὸ θεῖον πνεῦμα καὶ τοὺς ἀπὸ τούτου λόγους διὰ τὸ τοῦ βίου δυσμίμητον καὶ σφόδρα εὔτονον καὶ ἐλευθέριον καὶ πάντῃ πρὸς θάνατον καὶ κινδύνους ἀκατάπληκτον. τοιούτους γὰρ καὶ ὁ λόγος αἱρεῖ δεῖν εἶναι τοὺς τοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσι θεοῦ προφήτας. οἵτινες παίγνιον ἀπέφηναν τὴν Ἀντισθένους καὶ Κράτητος καὶ Διογένους εὐτονίαν. δι᾿ ἀλήθειαν γοῦν καὶ τὸ ἐλευθερίως ἐλέγχειν τοὺς ἁμαρτάνοντας „ἐλιθάσθησαν, ἐπρίσθησαν, ἐπειράσθησαν, ἐν φόνῳ μαχαίρας ἀπέθανον· περιῆλθον γὰρ ἐν μηλωταῖς, ἐν αἰγείοις δέρμασιν, ὑστερούμενοι, κακουχούμενοι, ἐν ἐρημίαις πλανώμενοι καὶ ὄρεσι καὶ σπηλαίοις καὶ ταῖς ὀπαῖς τῆς γῆς, ὧν οὐκ ην ἄξιος ὁ ἐπὶ γῆς κόσμος“· ἀεὶ ἐνορῶντες τῷ θεῷ καὶ τοῖς ἀοράτοις τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ μὴ βλεπομένοις αἰσθητῶς καὶ διὰ τοῦτο οὖσιν αἰωνίοις. ὁ δὲ βίος ἑκάστου τῶν προφητῶν ἀναγέγραπται· ἀρκεῖ δὲ ἐπὶ τοῦ παρόντος παραθέσθαι τὸν Μωϋσέως βίον (καὶ γὰρ αὐτοῦ φέρονται προφητεῖαι, ἀναγεγραμμέναι ἐν τῷ νόμῳ) καὶ τὸν Ἱερεμἰου, φερόμενον ἐν τῇ ὁμωνύμῳ αὐτοῦ προφητείᾳ, καὶ τὸν Ἡσαΐου, ὃς ἐπορεύθη ὑπερτείνων πᾶσαν ἄσκησιν „γυμνὸς καὶ ἀνυπόδετος“ ἔτεσι τρισίν. ἴδε δὲ καὶ παιδαρίων, τοῦ Δανιὴλ καὶ τῶν σὺν αὐτῷ, τὸν ἐῤῥωμένον βίον, ἀναγνοὺς τὴν ὑδροποσίαν αὐτῶν καὶ ὅτι ἡ τροφὴ ἦν αὐτοῖς ὄσπριον, ἐμψύχων ἀπεχομένοις. εἰ δὲ δύνασαι, καὶ τὰ πρὸ τούτων θέασαι, Νῶε προφητεύσαντος καὶ Ἰσαὰκ τῷ υἱῷ ἐπευξαμένου προφητικῶς καὶ τοῦ Ἰακὼβ λέγοντος ἑκάστῳ τῶν δώδεκα· „δεῦτε, ἵνα ἀναγγείλω ὑμῖν, τί ἔσται ἐπ᾿ ἐσχάτων τῶν ἡμερῶν.“ οὗτοι δὴ καὶ ἄλλοι μυρίοι προφητεύσαντες τῷ θεῷ καὶ τὰ περὶ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ Χριστοῦ προεῖπον. διόπερ ἐν οὐδενὶ μὲν τιθέμεθα λόγῳ τὰ ὑπὸ τῆς Πυθίας ἢ Δωδωνίδων ἢ Κλαρίου ἢ ἐν Βραγχίδαις ἢ ἐν Ἄμμωνος ἢ ὑπὸ μυρίων ἄλλων λεγομένων θεοπρόπων προειρημένα· τὰ δ᾿ ὑπὸ τῶν ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ προφητευσάντων τεθήπαμεν, ὁρῶντες ὅτι ἄξιος ἦν αὐτῶν ὁ ἐῤῥωμένος καὶ εὔτονος καὶ σεμνὸς βίος πνεύματος θεοῦ, τρόπῳ προφητεύοντος καινῷ καὶ οὐδὲν ἔχοντι παραπλήσιον ταῖς ἀπὸ δαιμόνων μαντείαις.
pass_a_gloss: Of the prophets among the Jews, some before the prophecy and the divine inspiration were wise, but others from the prophecy itself, having been enlightened in the mind, became such, having been chosen by providence to believe in the divine Spirit and the words from it, because of the unpleasant and very strenuous and free and in every way fearless of death and dangers life. For the Word chooses such to be the prophets of the God over all. Who made a mockery of the endurance of Antisthenes and Crates and Diogenes. For through truth and freely reproving those sinning, they were stoned, sawed, tempted, died by the sword; for they walked in sheepskins, in goatskins, being destitute, afflicted, wandering in deserts and mountains and caves and the holes of the earth, of whom the world was not worthy; always looking to God and the invisible things of God and not seen sensibly and therefore being eternal. The life of each of the prophets is written; but it is enough for the present to set forth the life of Moses (for prophecies of him are also borne, written in the law) and the life of Jeremiah, borne in his own prophecy, and the life of Isaiah, who went beyond all asceticism, naked and barefoot for three years. See also the life of the children, of Daniel and those with him, having read their abstinence from drink and that their food was vegetables, abstaining from flesh. But if you are able, also look at those before these, Noah prophesying and Isaac having prayed prophetically to his son and Jacob saying to each of the twelve: 'Come, that I may announce to you what will be in the last days.' These, then, and many others, having prophesied to God, also spoke about Jesus the Christ. Wherefore we do not put the words spoken by the Pythia or the Dodonian oracles or Clarian or in Branchidae or in Ammon or by the myriads of other so-called prophets in any account; but the things spoken by those who prophesied in Judaea we have set forth, seeing that the strenuous and free and dignified life of the Spirit of God was worthy of them, prophesying in a new way and having nothing similar to the divinations from demons.
pass_b_english: Among the Jewish prophets, some were wise before they ever received prophecy or divine inspiration, while others were enlightened through the very act of prophesying and became that kind of person. They were chosen by providence to trust the divine Spirit and the words that come from it, because their manner of life is disagreeable, extremely demanding, and free—utterly undaunted by death and danger in every respect. For the Word chooses just such people to serve as prophets of the God over all.

These prophets made a mockery of the famed endurance of Antisthenes, Crates, and Diogenes. Because they spoke the truth and freely rebuked sinners, they were stoned, sawn in two, tempted, and killed by the sword. They wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, and mistreated—roaming deserts and mountains, hiding in caves and holes in the ground. The world was not worthy of them (Hebrews 11:37-38). They kept their eyes fixed on God and on the invisible realities of God—things not perceived by the senses—and for that reason those realities are eternal.

The life of each prophet is recorded, but for our present purpose it is enough to set forth the life of Moses (since his prophecies are also preserved, written in the Law), the life of Jeremiah (preserved in the prophecy that bears his name), and the life of Isaiah, who surpassed all asceticism by going naked and barefoot for three years. Consider also the vigorous life of the youths—Daniel and his companions—by reading of their abstinence from wine and the fact that their food was vegetables, since they avoided meat. If you are able, look further back at those who came before: Noah prophesying, Isaac praying prophetically over his son, and Jacob addressing each of his twelve sons: 'Come, that I may tell you what will happen in the last days.' These, and many thousands of others, prophesied to God and also foretold the things concerning Jesus the Christ.

Therefore we give no credence whatever to the words spoken by the Pythia, the Dodonian oracles, the Clarian oracle, the shrine at Branchidae, the oracle of Ammon, or by the myriads of other so-called prophets. But we do set forth the words spoken by those who prophesied in Judaea, because we see that their strenuous, free, and dignified life—empowered by the Spirit of God—was worthy of them. They prophesied in a new way that bears no resemblance whatever to the divinations that come from demons.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the Greek text. Pass B correctly identifies the allusion to Hebrews 11:37-38 for the description of the prophets' sufferings, which is a required addition for clarity in patristic studies. All clauses, including the specific list of prophets and the comparison to pagan oracles, are preserved.
